content.title: About
content.content: Marie biscuit is a light, dry biscuit originally created in the United Kingdom in 1874. It has a delicate buttery flavor, crisp texture, and a characteristic square shape. The biscuit is often enjoyed as a simple snack, with tea or milk, and is also used in desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original Marie biscuit was named after Princess Marie, daughter of King Edward VII.
It quickly became popular in the Soviet Union, where it was a staple in school cafeterias.
The classic recipe uses wheat flour, vegetable oil, sugar, and a leavening agent.
Marie biscuits are frequently used as a base for "torte" and cheesecake recipes.
In some countries the biscuit is sold under different brand names but retains the same formula.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Marie biscuits contain a modest amount of fat, making them suitable for moderate consumption in low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The carbohydrates provide quick energy, useful for a light snack.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Small amounts of vitamins B1 and B2 support normal metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture allows rapid digestion without heavy stomach load.

items.title: Kid‑friendly
items.content: Small size and mild texture make the biscuit convenient for children (when no allergy is present).

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Marie biscuits contain sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Made with wheat flour, the biscuit is not suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: Some versions may contain flavorings or preservatives that could trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marie biscuits can be eaten plain, dipped in tea, milk, or coffee. They are often used in desserts: crushed for a cake base, added to ice cream, or prepared as a milk‑pudding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the biscuits in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crispness.
